papers_checked.title: Atomically Dispersed Fe-N4 Modified with Precisely Located S for Highly Efficient Oxygen Reduction
papers_checked.configurations_found: Fe-N4 in a graphene divacancy (4x4 cell, two C removed, four N), with S placed in the second shell at three different positions (models named Fe-N4S1-C, Fe-N4S2-C, Fe-N4S3-C, where the subscript is the position, not a count), plus S-free Fe-N4 (Fe-NC). EXAFS fit gives about four N around Fe. No Fe-S bond in the first shell and no three-coordinate Fe.
papers_checked.evidence: Full text from PubMed Central (PMC7770948): the methods describe removing two carbon atoms and substituting four C atoms around the divacancy with four N atoms. The carbon atoms next to and opposite the Fe-N4 moiety were replaced by S. EXAFS gives 'average four N atoms' around Fe, in a Fe(N4)(N-C-S) configuration.

motifs.her_note: None of the checked papers computes hydrogen evolution for Fe-NS2. The Fe N/S series compute other reactions: CO2 reduction (FeNnS4-n, 10.1002/cplu.202300306), ORR/OER (FeSxN4-x, 10.1002/cssc.202300637), ORR (Fe-N4 with second-shell S, 10.1007/s40820-020-00456-8; Fe-N3S1 papers) and NRR (TM-S4-G, 10.1021/acs.jpclett.2c02105). The HER-focused graphene SAC papers found (e.g. 10.1039/d4ra09113b, 10.1002/cphc.70486, 10.1039/d6cp01369d) did not show N+S co-coordinated Fe in their titles. Our dG_H = -0.20 eV for Fe-NS2 therefore has no direct literature comparison.
motifs.summary: The only full text that could be read, Nano-Micro Lett. 10.1007/s40820-020-00456-8 (via PMC), computes Fe-N4 in a divacancy with S only in the second shell. The two DFT family screenings, 10.1002/cplu.202300306 (FeNnS4-n, n = 1-4) and 10.1002/cssc.202300637 (FeSxN4-x, x = 1-4), could only be checked at abstract level because Wiley returned 403. Their stated series contain only four-coordinate FeN3S1, FeN2S2 and FeN1S3, not three-coordinate FeN1S2. Citation listings for both papers, similar papers to the closest one, and searches by series notation (N3-xSx, FeNS2, FeN2S, N2S1, TM-N2S/NS2 in a single vacancy) found only Fe-N3S1(-OH), TM-S4-G, Fe-N cluster and non-Fe screenings, so Fe-NS2 stays related_only. Confidence is medium because the tables and SI of the two screenings and of the Gallagher 3d-TM/S-dopant screening (10.1039/d4cp04212c) could not be read.

papers_checked.configurations_found: M-N4-xOx embedded in graphene, M = Fe, Co, Ni, x = 1-4. For Fe that covers Fe-N3O1, Fe-N2O2, Fe-N1O3 and Fe-O4. The abstract highlights Co-N3O1 and Ni-N2O2 as the best ORR catalysts.
papers_checked.evidence: The journal page (journal.hep.com.cn/fcse) abstract reads: 'the detailed oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) catalytic performance of M-N4-xOx (M= Fe, Co, and Ni; x = 1-4)'. The full text of the Molecules 2023 paper (PMC10650445, ref. 20) independently cites it as M-N4-xOx (M=Fe, Co, Ni; x = 1-4) and names Co-N3O1 and Ni-N2O2 as the most active. The paper is closed access (OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar both say CLOSED; Springer redirects to a login). So I could not see the Fe-N1O3 table entry, its stability, or whether the site is a double vacancy, although 'M-N4 embedded graphene' is normally the DV MN4 site. The paper studies ORR only, not HER.

motifs.her_note: No checked paper reports HER for Fe-N1O3. Ge et al. 2021, the only paper that covers Fe-N1O3 (the x = 3 member of its series), computed ORR only. The HER papers I found are a different site (FeN2O2 on graphene, dG_H* = 0.09 eV, NJC 2026, closed access, so other N/O ratios cannot be excluded) and a different motif (TM-NO2 anchored graphene, ChemPhysChem 2026, best Ni-NO2 at -0.39 eV). Our Fe-NO3 dG_H = -0.12 eV therefore appears new as an HER result, but the motif itself is not new.
motifs.summary: The verdict changes from not_found/related_only to reported_computational_only. The 2021 paper by Ge, Qiao, Chen and Wu (10.1007/s11705-020-2017-7) computes M-N4-xOx embedded in graphene for M = Fe, Co, Ni and x = 1-4, which includes Fe-N1O3 (x = 3); the journal abstract and the Molecules 2023 full text (10.3390/molecules28217264, ref. 20) both state this, but the Ge full text is closed, so the Fe-N1O3 table entry, its stability and the exact double-vacancy geometry are unverified (confidence medium). No checked paper computes HER on Fe-N1O3 (Ge et al. is ORR only), and the nearest HER papers are FeN2O2 on graphene (NJC 2026, 10.1039/d6nj00842a, closed access) and TM-NO2 anchored graphene (ChemPhysChem 2026, 10.1002/cphc.70486), so the HER result for this motif looks new while the motif does not.

papers_checked.title: Axial Oxygen Ligands Regulating Electronic and Geometric Structure of Zn-N-C Sites to Boost Oxygen Reduction Reaction
papers_checked.configurations_found: DFT (Fig. 1a): Zn-N4 (Eb -1.97 eV); Zn-N4-O with O bonded only to Zn (axial, -1.14 eV); Zn-N4-O with O bridging Zn and N (-1.34 eV). They report that under ORR the Zn-N4-O site evolves into Zn-N3-O when an adsorbate is bound and reverts once *OH desorbs. Experiment (EXAFS): Zn-N4 and Zn-N4-O (CN 4.8) on N-doped carbon.
papers_checked.evidence: PMC full text (WebFetch of PMC10460851): 'the adsorption of the reaction intermediates induces the structural evolution of Zn-N4-O to Zn-N3-O under ORR working conditions'. This Zn-N3-O exists only with a bound ORR intermediate and an out-of-plane bridging O, so it is not a bare in-plane Zn-N3O site.

papers_checked.title: Boosted hydrogen evolution kinetics of heteroatom-doped carbons with isolated Zn as an accelerant

papers_checked.evidence: PMC10835066 full text: 'Two proposed models, including planar symmetrical ZnN4 moiety with a subsurface S atom ... and planar unsymmetrical ZnN3S moiety with a subsurface N atom'. Zn–N CN ~4.1 and Zn–S ~1.0.

papers_checked.title: Computational Screening of Single-Metal-Atom Embedded Graphene-Based Electrocatalysts Stabilized by Heteroatoms (Cho et al., Front. Chem. 2022)
papers_checked.configurations_found: MX4 and MYX3 sites in a graphene double vacancy for 28 metals (3d Sc–Zn, 4d Y–Cd, 5d Hf–Au) with X, Y from B, N, O, P, S. That is 700 combinations, which includes Zn-ON3 (= Zn-N3O). Formation energies were computed for all of them as the first filter: 222 were stable and 66 were carried through ORR (*OOH, *O, *OH). Zn-N4 is discussed explicitly. Zn-ON3 is not named in the text.
papers_checked.evidence: Frontiers full text (WebFetch): screening of '3d (from Sc to Zn), 4d (from Y to Cd), and 5d (from Hf to Au)' metals and '700 possible combinations (= 28 transition metals × 5 host heteroatoms × 5 dopant heteroatoms)'; 'the Co-ON3 structure comprises a Co atom fourfold coordinated with one O atom and three N atoms in the presence of two C vacancies'; 'First, we obtained structural stability based on the formation energy, and then the stable structures were filtered out'. ORR only, no HER/*H. Whether Zn-ON3 passed the stability filter was not stated in the fetched text (likely only in a figure or the SI).

motifs.her_note: No checked paper computes HER (ΔG_H*) on Zn-N3O. Cho et al. 2022 screened Zn-ON3 for ORR only. Jin et al. 2023 (Zn-N4-O → Zn-N3-O) is ORR only. The only Zn HER paper among those checked (PNAS 2024) uses ZnN4S1/ZnN3S models with H adsorption on neighbouring N/C sites. So our ΔG_H = +0.12 eV for Zn-N3O in a double vacancy appears to be new as an HER result.
motifs.summary: The verdict changes from 'not reported' to reported_computational_only. Cho et al. (Front. Chem. 2022, 10.3389/fchem.2022.873609) screened MX4/MYX3 sites in a graphene double vacancy for 28 metals including Zn and the O/N combination. Their method computes formation energies for all 700 combinations, so Zn-ON3 (= Zn-N3O) was calculated, although the main text does not name it and does not say whether it passed their stability filter. Jin et al. (Adv. Sci. 2023, 10.1002/advs.202302152) see Zn-N3-O only as an adsorbate-bound ORR intermediate of Zn-N4-O (related, not exact). The full texts of Molecules 2023 (Zn-N2O2, molecular ligand) and PNAS 2024 (ZnN4S1/ZnN3S, HER) contain no Zn-N3O. No paper reports Zn-N3O experimentally or computes HER on it.

papers_checked.title: Construction of Single-Atom Catalysts for N, O Synergistic Coordination and Application to Electrocatalytic O2 Reduction
papers_checked.configurations_found: Only TM-N2O2C14 (TM = Sc to Zn, Co included): 'each transition metal atom coordinates with two nitrogen atoms and two oxygen atoms simultaneously'. This is a framework built from a 4-hydroxybenzonitrile ligand, not graphene. No Co-C bond and no N2OC variant. The introduction cites Ge et al., M-NxO4-x (M = Fe, Co, Ni; x = 1-4), which also has no C in the first shell.
papers_checked.evidence: Full text from PMC10650445: the unit cell 'contains one transition metal atom, two nitrogen atoms, two oxygen atoms, fourteen carbon atoms, and eight hydrogen atoms'. The only reaction studied is ORR. The PubMed subscripts were stripped and are read here from that atom count.

papers_checked.title: Identification of catalytic sites in cobalt-nitrogen-carbon materials for the oxygen reduction reaction
papers_checked.configurations_found: Co sites with N only (pyridinic CoN4C10 and CoN4C8, porphyrinic CoN4C12 and their defective CoN3C10 and CoN2C5 forms, plus other pyridinic-defective variants), each with or without an end-on O2 adsorbate (O2-CoN2C5 and similar). No lattice O and no Co-C first-shell bond.
papers_checked.evidence: Full text from PMC5715157: XANES and DFT-D candidates are the porphyrinic CoN4C12 family 'derived ... by subtracting one or two nitrogen atoms' (subscripts stripped in the PMC text and taken from the known paper notation). The O in O-CoN2C5 is an adsorbed O2 molecule, not a framework donor. HER was measured experimentally on the material but was not linked to any O/C-containing site.

papers_checked.title: Atomically dispersed asymmetric cobalt electrocatalyst for efficient hydrogen peroxide production in neutral media
papers_checked.configurations_found: Experiment: Co-C/N/O on N-doped carbon black, where EXAFS could not settle the exact shell. DFT: 'eight C4v-alike asymmetric configurations with five Co-C/N/O coordination paths'. Named in the text: CoN2O2-C (5-coordinate). Reported EXAFS fitting paths: Co-N3/O2, Co-N1/N2 with split shells, Co-C3/N2, all 5-coordinate. The other 7 DFT models appear only in Fig. 5d and SI Fig. S22, which I could not read.
papers_checked.evidence: PMC11093996 text: 'eight C-alike asymmetric configurations with five Co-C/N/O coordination paths were proposed' and 'Most configuration models except CoN2O2-C were located at the left side of the volcano plot'. A WebFetch of the PMC HTML gave the subscripts. nature.com redirected to a login page and the PMC figure page showed a CAPTCHA, so I could not check SI Fig. S22. This paper uses the same elements in a 5-coordinate, C4v-like shell, which is closely related but not the 4-coordinate N2OC motif. Only 2e- ORR is studied, not HER.

papers_checked.configurations_found: OCoN2C2: penta-coordinated Co with 2 N, 2 C and 1 O (experiment plus DFT). The CoN4 reference is mentioned. No full text, so any other DFT models are unknown.
papers_checked.evidence: Abstract (PubMed 35324078): 'penta-coordinated CoNC configuration (OCoN2C2) with Co center coordinated by two nitrogen atoms, two carbon atoms, and one oxygen atom'. Wiley full text returned HTTP 403 and there is no PMC copy. This has one more C than our motif, so it is related only. Only 2e- ORR is studied.

motifs.her_note: I found no paper that studies HER on a Co-N2OC site. Two papers do study HER on related sites. Small 2022 (10.1002/smll.202201139) covers Co-N3 and Co-N4 in graphene with no O. ChemPhysChem 2026 (10.1002/cphc.70486) covers TM-NO2 anchored on graphene. Nat Commun 2017 (10.1038/s41467-017-01100-7) measured HER experimentally on a Co-N-C material with CoNxCy sites, again with no O/C mixed shell. Every Co paper with N plus O in the first shell (Small 2022 OCoN2C2, JPCL 2025 Co-N3O, Angew 2025 Co-NxO4-x, Nat Commun 2024 Co-C/N/O, Molecules 2023 TM-N2O2C14) studies ORR or 2e- ORR, not HER. Our dG_H = +0.03 eV therefore has no direct literature comparison.
motifs.summary: None of the papers I read in full or as abstracts shows a Co atom with exactly 2 N, 1 O and 1 C in its first shell on a carbon support. The closest are Small 2022 (10.1002/smll.202200730), which has 5-coordinate OCoN2C2; Nat Commun 2024 (10.1038/s41467-024-48209-0), which models eight 5-coordinate Co-C/N/O sites, with only CoN2O2-C named in the text; and the Co-NxO4-x and TM-N2O2C14 series (Angew 2025, 10.1002/anie.202416070; Molecules 2023, 10.3390/molecules28217264), which have no C donor. The verdict stays related_only at medium confidence, because the full model list in Nat Commun 2024 SI Fig. S22 and the full texts of Small 2022, JPCL 2025 Co-N3O and PCCP 2024 TM-N2X (which computes 3-coordinate Co-N2O and Co-N2C) were blocked (CAPTCHA, HTTP 403 or no PMC copy) and should be checked by hand.

motifs.her_note: I found no paper that computes dG_H (or any HER quantity) for Mo-NS3. HER/dG_H data exist only for related motifs: M@SxNy-graphene including S3N1 for Mn/Fe/Co (10.3390/nano12234309, full text); H adsorption on Mo-NxPy-graphene, where HER is the competing reaction (10.1039/d4na00298a, full text); and experimental HER on Mo1N1C2 (10.1002/anie.201710599, prior note). For Mo-S4-G (10.1021/acs.jpclett.2c02105) the abstract covers NRR only. Its SI, which might hold H* data, was not accessible.
motifs.summary: None of the checked papers computes or makes Mo with exactly one N and three S on a carbon support. The only full-text Mo screening that could be read, Khedr et al. 2024 (10.1039/d4na00298a, PMC11304078), covers Mo-NxPy (x+y=4), with no S anywhere. The closest series-notation paper, Ritopečki et al. 2022 (10.3390/nano12234309, PMC9737643), computes the exact S3N1 di-vacancy pattern only for Mn, Fe and Co, so it is related only. The most likely hidden source, the TM-S4-G screening by Wen et al. 2022 (10.1021/acs.jpclett.2c02105, Mo-S4 among 25 metals), was abstract-only, like the Mo/S-doped graphene PCCP 2019 paper (10.1039/c9cp02733e) and the Mo O,S Angewandte 2020 paper (10.1002/anie.202003842); their publisher pages returned 403. Their SI therefore remains an unchecked gap, which is why confidence is medium. The citing lists of 10.1021/acs.jpclett.2c02105 and 10.1039/c9cp02733e, the papers similar to 10.1021/acs.jpclett.2c02105, and the series-notation searches (MoN4-xSx, N1S3, NS3, MoN3S/MoN2S2/MoNS3) turned up no Mo-NS3 paper. Budget used: 12 searches or listings, 6 abstracts, and 5 full-text attempts (2 succeeded, 3 were blocked) plus one retry after a rate limit.

motifs.her_note: No checked paper computes hydrogen evolution or dG_H for Fe-S2C2. The nearest HER-related work is Ritopečki et al. 2022 (10.3390/nano12234309), which computes hydrogen reactivity for Fe@SxNy (S/N, not S/C). The 2026 review summarises that work as finding Fe SACs where O- or S-doping can enhance HER activity but are mostly unstable. Our +0.21 eV for Fe-S2C2 has no direct literature comparison in the papers checked.
motifs.summary: The two papers whose full texts were readable show no Fe-S2C2. The 2026 review by van Dam and Vermeeren (10.1039/d6cp00932h, PMC13248922) lists mixed C shells only for N and O (Fe-NxCy, Fe-OxCy, Fe-2N2CDG), and S only as Fe-4SDG or S/N mixtures. The screening by Cho, Park and Han (10.3389/fchem.2022.873609, PMC9019222) computes only M-X4 and M-YX3 with X, Y in {B, N, O, P, S}, so there is no C in the Fe first shell. From abstracts only, the closest papers report FeNnS4-n (10.1002/cplu.202300306), TM-S4 (10.1021/acs.jpclett.2c02105), Fe@SxNy (10.3390/nano12234309) and C/N-only shells (10.1039/d6dt01022a), so the verdict stays related_only. Confidence is medium, not high, because the full texts and SI of the Hadsadee, Wen, Gallagher/Zhao, Balderramas Morgan and ChemSusChem FeSxN4-x papers could not be read (HTTP 403 or no PMC copy), and the Tang TM-4XDG study cited in the review was not found.

issues.problem: The verdicts are not consistent across reports. The Zn-N3O report upgrades its motif to reported_computational_only because Cho et al. (Front. Chem. 2022, 10.3389/fchem.2022.873609) computed formation energies for all 700 MX4/MYX3 combinations in a graphene double vacancy. That set covers 28 metals (Sc-Zn, Y-Cd, Hf-Au) and X, Y from {B, N, O, P, S}, with MYX3 meaning 1 Y + 3 X. The Fe-S2C2 report read this full text (PMC9019222) and confirms the M-X4/M-YX3 scope. Mo is a 4d metal, so Mo with Y = N and X = S (Mo-NS3, 1 N + 3 S in a double vacancy) is in the computed set. The Mo-NS3 report never checked this paper and kept related_only.
